newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral to keep most of outgoing cabinet.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral to keep most of outgoing cabinet.

text.p: Indian prime minister-designate Inder Kumar Gujral has decided to retain most ministers in the government of his predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda, an aide to President Shankar Dayal Sharma said on Monday.
But P. Chidambaram, outgoing finance minister, will not retain the post, the aide, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
"The entire cabinet is being retained except for Chidambaram and Arunachalam," the aide said, referring to Labour Minister M. Arunachalam.

Chidambaram's regional Tamil Maanila Congress party decided on Saturday not to join Gujral's government after the United Front coalition passed over its leader, G.K. Moopanar, and chose Gujral instead as its chief.
Gujral, 77, was scheduled to be sworn in as the nation's 12th prime minister later on Monday.
